_note: Hand-written building blocks for player and official profiles (UNIVERSO-SPEC section 2): nicknames with their origin, playing styles and strengths, curiosities, injuries and referee notes. Written in English with Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code; every text is original and names no real person. The generator fills the {placeholders} from the player's own data, so a curiosity never contradicts the universe. Each nickname and each curiosity is used at most once per squad.

nicknames.origin: At {height} cm he towers over every penalty box like a lighthouse over a harbour; a team-mate at {first_club} came up with it.
Youth coaches at {first_club} gave him the name because he wore his goalkeeper gloves to every session, even to lunch.
For the spring in his legs: he can touch the crossbar from a standing jump.
A striker at {first_club} said that trying to get past him was like running into brickwork.
Because he never drifts from his post in front of the defence.
For the accuracy of his long passing; team-mates say he finds them before they know they are free.
For his reading of the game and his habit of explaining tactics to younger team-mates on the team bus.
Because he keeps running long after everyone else has stopped.
For his acceleration over the first five metres.
For a left foot that bends the ball around defenders.
For the way he sniffs out chances in the six-yard box.
For the way he hovers on the edge of the box, waiting to pounce.
Because he always delivers; it started when he scored in his first game for {first_club}.
For the energy he brings to the pitch; his first coach said he played like a box of matches.
He was the youngest player in the dressing room when he made his debut, and the name stuck.
For his consistency: coaches say he has not had a bad game in years.
Because loose balls always seem to end up at his feet.
For the power of his shooting from distance.
Because he hardly says a word in the dressing room, but his team-mates always hear him on the pitch.
For the steady rhythm of his passing.
For the way he twists and turns past defenders.
For his strength in the air and on the ground.
Because he organises everyone around him, on and off the pitch.
For the way he drifts into space without defenders noticing.
For his long throw-ins, which fly almost to the penalty spot.
For his close control in tight spaces.
At {height} cm he was the tallest outfield player his youth coaches at {first_club} had ever seen.
At {height} cm he is small enough, team-mates joke, to fit in the coach's pocket.
For the way he follows his direct opponent everywhere.
For his runs down the wing, which leave a trail of defenders behind him.
After his hometown of {town} and his speed on the counter-attack.
Supporters of {first_club} gave him the name because he was the first player from {town} to reach their first team in years.
To tell him apart from a smaller namesake in the {first_club} youth team.

surname_nickname_origins: A dressing-room shortening of his surname that has followed him since his academy days at {first_club}.
Short for his surname; a youth coach at {first_club} started it and nobody has used his full name since.
The squad shortened his surname on his first day at {first_club}, and it stuck.
initials_nickname_origin: His initials, which the squad has used since a kit mix-up put them on his training top at {first_club}.

GK.shot-stopper: A shot-stopper with quick reflexes who commands his six-yard box.
GK.sweeper-keeper: A sweeper-keeper who starts attacks with his feet and is comfortable far off his line.

CB.aerial: A commanding centre back who wins almost everything in the air and is a threat at set pieces.
CB.ball-playing: A ball-playing centre back who steps into midfield and breaks lines with his passing.
CB.stopper: A traditional stopper: aggressive in the tackle and happiest marking the opposition's main striker.

FB.overlapping: An attacking full back who overlaps the winger and delivers crosses on the run.
FB.defensive: A defensive full back who keeps his position and rarely loses a one-against-one duel.
FB.inverted: An inverted full back who moves into midfield when his team has the ball.

DM.ball-winner: A ball-winning midfielder who breaks up play in front of the defence.
DM.deep playmaker: A deep-lying playmaker who sets the tempo with short and long passes.

CM.box-to-box: A box-to-box midfielder who covers every blade of grass and arrives late in the box.
CM.playmaker: A creative central midfielder who looks for the forward pass at every chance.
CM.engine: A tireless midfield engine who presses high and keeps the team's shape.

AM.creator: A classic number 10 who creates chances between the lines.
AM.second striker: A second striker who plays off the centre forward and attacks the space behind the defence.

W.pacy: A pacy winger who loves to run at full backs.
W.inverted: An inverted winger who cuts inside onto his stronger foot to shoot or pass.
W.crosser: A traditional winger who stays wide and delivers early crosses.

ST.poacher: A penalty-box striker who lives on the last defender's shoulder.
ST.target man: A target man who holds the ball up and brings team-mates into play.
ST.pressing forward: A pressing forward who leads the press from the front and works the channels.

second_style: He can also play the role of {style}.

curiosities.text: He wears number {shirt} because it was the number of the bus that took him to training as a teenager.
He keeps the boots he wore on his senior debut for {first_club}, in {first_season}, in a glass case at home.
He is studying for a degree in sports science by distance learning.
He is a keen chess player and organises a squad tournament every pre-season.
Before turning professional he worked weekends in his family's bakery in {town}.
He plays the trumpet and still joins the {town} community band at Christmas.
He was a regional 400 m champion as a teenager before choosing football.
He collects old matchday programmes and owns one from the first Estuary Derby in 1896.
He reads a book on every away trip and shares a reading list with his team-mates.
He trained as an electrician before football took off.
He takes a photo of every stadium the first time he plays there.
He volunteers at a youth football project in {town} every summer.
He is a qualified swimming instructor.
He has written a children's book about a lighthouse keeper's dog.
He keeps a notebook on every direct opponent he faces.
He is a keen birdwatcher and can name every bird on the estuary.
He cooks breakfast for the whole squad on the morning of away games.
He took the referees' course to understand the laws better, and passed with top marks.
He cycles to training every day, whatever the weather.
He plays the piano and wrote the walk-out music for the academy's summer tournament.
He learned the club anthem by heart before he signed.
He still lives on the street in {town} where he grew up.
He is the third generation of his family to play professional football.
His first senior goal was a header, even though he is one of the shorter players in the squad.
He grows his own vegetables and brings the best tomatoes to the training ground.
He paints landscapes of the estuary in his free time; one of them hangs in the club museum.
He has a pet tortoise named after his first youth coach.
He never wears gloves, even on the coldest winter nights.
He speaks four languages.
He learned the Meridian language in six months and now gives interviews without an interpreter.
He moved to Meridia at {debut_age} and lived with a host family during his first season at {first_club}.
During his loan at {loan_club} he lived with a local family who still come to watch him play.
He was a ball boy at the {club_ground} before he signed his first contract.
He joined the {club} academy at the age of eight.
He supported {first_club} as a boy and joined their academy at nine.
He played as a goalkeeper in junior football and only moved outfield at fourteen.
He played as a striker in junior football and only moved in goal at thirteen.
He saved a penalty on his senior debut for {first_club}.
He scored on his senior debut for {first_club} in {first_season}.
He became a father last season and celebrates his goals by rocking an imaginary cradle.
He was born in {town} and is the first player from the town to reach the Meridian League.
He is a keen sea swimmer and swims in the estuary all year round.
He was released by the {first_club} academy at fifteen and re-signed a year later after a trial.
He wears his socks rolled down, a habit from his days at {first_club}.
He runs a small coffee stall at the {town} market in the summer.
He is a qualified primary-school teacher.
He walks his dog along the harbour wall before every home game.
He knits his own scarves and gave one to every team-mate last winter.
He can solve a puzzle cube in under a minute.
He once played a whole match with a broken toe and only told the physio afterwards.
He collects the shirts of every opponent he has scored against.
He has a twin brother who is a schoolteacher in {town}.
He was spotted by a scout while playing beach football on holiday.
He brings his grandmother's lucky scarf to every away game.
He does the club's matchday crossword in the programme before every home game.
He learned to juggle a ball by practising against his grandparents' garage door every evening.
He keeps a jar of soil from every pitch where he has scored.
He is a qualified lifeguard and has worked summers on the beaches near {town}.
He designs his own boot colours and lets a different child from the academy choose them each season.
He has run the stadium stairs before every pre-season since his first year as a professional.
He learned sign language to talk with a deaf cousin and now teaches a few signs to team-mates.
He writes a short letter to his younger self after every season and keeps them all in a box.
He grew up on a farm and still helps with the harvest in the summer break.
He is a keen astronomer and brings a telescope on summer training camps.
He once scored a goal in a charity match while wearing a full lamplighter's costume.
He hosts a monthly reading club at the local library for children.
He builds model ships and has a replica of the estuary ferry in his living room.
He was the head boy at his secondary school in {town}.
He has completed three marathons and wants to run one in every country he has lived in.
He plays the drums in a band with old school friends.
He studied architecture for a year before signing his first professional contract.
He is an expert on the history of his first club, {first_club}, and has written articles for its fan magazine.
He organises a five-a-side tournament in {town} every summer for local charities.
He keeps bees and gives jars of honey to the kit room staff.
He was named after the hospital nurse who helped deliver him.
He has never missed a team photo, even the year he had a broken arm.
He speaks to the dressing room before every derby, a habit started by an old team-mate.
He collects old maps and can name every lighthouse along the coast.
He does yoga every morning and leads the stretching session before training.
He trains with a ballet teacher once a week to improve his balance.

officials.referee_strict: Refereed the 2025/26 Meridian Cup final. A strict referee: he shows more cards per game than the panel average and is quick to punish dissent.
officials.referee_lenient: Refereed the 2025/26 Meridian Cup final. He likes to let the game flow: he shows fewer cards per game than the panel average and talks to players a lot.
officials.video_assistant_referee: A top-division referee who now mostly works as video assistant referee; he led the VAR team at the 2024/25 Meridian Cup final.
officials.fourth_official: An experienced top-division referee who often works as fourth official in derbies.
officials.assistant_video_assistant_referee: A former assistant referee, now a specialist in the video room.
officials.assistant_referee_1: Ran the line at the 2023/24 Meridian Cup final and is known for accurate offside calls.
officials.assistant_referee_2: One of the youngest assistants on the national panel; he works most derbies with the same refereeing team.
